from PIL import Image
import numpy as np

img44 = np.array(Image.open("/work/observations/obs_0044.png"))

# In obs 42, camera was at (0.7071, 5.2071) facing +x
# In obs 44, camera is at (1.2071, 4.7071) facing +x
# Lamp base in obs 44:
mask_base = (img44[:,:,0] > 50) & (img44[:,:,0] < 120) & (img44[:,:,1] > 60) & (img44[:,:,1] < 120) & (img44[:,:,2] > 80) & (img44[:,:,2] < 140) & (np.arange(512)[:, None] > 400)
coords = np.argwhere(mask_base)
print("Obs 44 Lamp base y:", coords[:,0].min(), coords[:,0].max(), "x:", coords[:,1].min(), coords[:,1].max())

# Pole center:
pole = np.argwhere((img44[:,:,0] > 50) & (img44[:,:,0] < 100) & (img44[:,:,1] > 60) & (img44[:,:,1] < 100) & (img44[:,:,2] > 70) & (img44[:,:,2] < 110) & (np.arange(512)[:, None] > 300) & (np.arange(512)[:, None] < 450))
print("Obs 44 Pole center x:", pole[:,1].mean())

# Let us find base ellipse in obs 44
# Forward is +x, Right is -y
# Ground contact y:
d = 396.8 / (coords[:,0].max() - 255.5)
xc = (pole[:,1].mean() - 255.5) / 256.0 * d
world_x = 1.2071 + d
world_y = 4.7071 - xc
print(f"Lamp base from obs 44: d={d:.3f}, x={world_x:.3f}, y={world_y:.3f}")
'
